question.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+14}{{x}^{2}-4}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}-9x+14}{{x}^{2}-4} \\  & =\frac{(x-7)(x-2)}{(x+2)(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{(x-7)\cancel{(x-2)}}{(x+2)\cancel{(x-2)}} \\  & =\frac{x-7}{x+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x-7 & =0\,⟹\,x=7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(x)=0$ is $x=7.$
